I specialise in Python and Bash scripting on Kali Linux and have built public tools and platforms such as CyberDict – a cybersecurity term dictionary – and CyberTools, a curated database of 600+ offensive and defensive toolscybertools.yanivhaliwa.com.My continuous learning includes completing TryHackMe’s Offensive Pentesting, Red Teaming, CompTIA PenTest+ and Jr Penetration Tester paths, ranking Guardian on Hack The Box (global rank ~5k, top‑60 in Israel), and finishing Advent of Cyber 2021–2024. I’m currently preparing for the Certified Penetration Testing Specialist (CPTS) exam.I love automating security workflows and sharing knowledge with the community. I’m looking for opportunities where I can combine red‑team work with tool development to help organisations stay ahead of threats.

אכלו לי את הראש עם הסוודרחבל שלינוקס לא עשו סוודר

I'm passionate about penetration testing - I probe every possible vulnerability, test every angle. And I'm equally passionate about Anthropic's Claude. So I built something that combines both: a Claude agent with access to every available Linux security tool, executing comprehensive penetration tests in a structured workflow. The tests run directly on my Linux machine. But what happens when I'm away from my computer? I built a bridge for full remote control of Claude AI through Telegram. How it works: 📱 Send message via Telegram → 🤖 Bot executes Claude CLI on my Linux machine → ⚡ 5 Hooks provide real-time updates on every step → 💬 Get complete response back What makes this special: ✅ Real-time updates on thinking process, tool execution, and results ✅ 60-minute session continuity ✅ Zero API costs - leverages existing Claude Pro OAuth ✅ Automatic state file cleanup after 30 seconds The result: A full-featured AI security assistant in my pocket - vulnerability scans, code analysis, exploit development, debugging - all accessible from Telegram. Oh, and I also use it for simple queries about files on my machine - Claude runs its BASH tools and delivers the answers. I asked Claude for its take on the project - including its response + a simple scan demonstration in the video. For the skeptics: Yes, I'm fully aware of the security implications of giving a bot access to my machine. No, you won't find the bot name - it's not publicly accessible. And even if you did, only my chat ID receives responses. But feel free to try. 😉 hashtag#CyberSecurity hashtag#AI hashtag#Automation hashtag#Python hashtag#Claude hashtag#PenetrationTesting hashtag#InfoSec hashtag#EthicalHacking
